insights.title: Card charge-off guidance lowered to 3.2%
insights.summary: Management guided the 2026 card net charge-off rate to about 3.4% on the Q4 2025 call and kept that figure on the Q1 2026 call. On the Q2 2026 call it was lowered to about 3.2%, attributed to better-than-expected consumer credit performance.
insights.uw_relevance: Card loss expectations are a core credit driver for a large card book. The revised figure is management's own forward view and is a point to test against delinquency and charge-off data.

insights.title: Consumer deposit growth outlook narrowed over 2026
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call management said 2026 consumer deposit growth was lower than its scenario analysis. On the Q1 2026 call the expected range was low to mid-single digits. On the Q2 2026 call it was low single-digit, with yield-seeking flows described as a continuing factor and probably a risk.
insights.uw_relevance: Deposit growth and funding stability bear on liquidity and funding risk for a bank. The narrowing of the stated range over three calls is a change in management's own funding outlook.

insights.title: SEC censure for supervision lapse, no fine
insights.summary: The SEC censured JPMorgan Chase and its securities unit for failing to supervise a statutorily disqualified person who traded in the US without permission from late 2021 to early 2024. No fine was imposed, but the SEC issued a cease-and-desist order. Other matters remain pending, including a South Africa inquiry and a India fine under appeal.
insights.uw_relevance: A supervisory failure finding with a cease-and-desist order is a regulatory conduct record relevant to D&O review of supervision and compliance controls, even without a monetary penalty.

followups.question: How does management plan to keep the CET1 ratio at its target level while preparing for the 5.2% G-SIB requirement in 2028, given the preliminary FY2026 Q3 CET1 ratio of 13.9%?
followups.summary: CET1 ratio was 14.2% in FY2026 Q2 and a preliminary 13.9% in FY2026 Q3, down from 15.7% in FY2024. Management said it must plan for a 5.2% G-SIB requirement in 2028, a 70 basis point rise from 4.5%.
followups.uw_relevance: A falling CET1 ratio combined with a higher required surcharge bears on the capital base and on how much capital the firm can return, which D&O reviewers weigh in capital-related exposure.

followups.question: What is the plan for funding stability as uninsured deposits rise and the average liquidity coverage ratio falls, and what share of uninsured balances is concentrated in the largest accounts?
followups.summary: Uninsured deposits were 64.3% of total deposits in FY2026 Q2, up from 60.9% in FY2025 Q4, an estimated $1,743.90B. The average liquidity coverage ratio was 110.0% in FY2026 Q2, against 112.0% in FY2026 Q1.
followups.uw_relevance: Rising uninsured deposit concentration and a lower coverage ratio bear directly on run risk and liquidity-related D&O exposure for a bank.

followups.question: What is driving the increase in the nonperforming loan ratio, and what supports the lower 2026 card net charge-off guidance of about 3.2%?
followups.summary: The nonperforming loan ratio was 0.7% at FY2025 Q4, up from 0.5% at FY2023 Q4. Management lowered its 2026 card net charge-off guidance to about 3.2% from about 3.4%, attributing the change to better-than-expected consumer credit performance.
followups.uw_relevance: Rising nonperforming loans alongside a lower charge-off assumption give a mixed credit picture that D&O reviewers need to test against delinquency and loss data.

followups.question: How large are the exposures in the private credit portion of the non-bank lending book, and what underwriting and covenant monitoring applies to loans where management reports weaker covenants and more rollover risk?
followups.summary: Core non-bank financial institution exposure is about $160 billion, of which about $50 billion is private credit. Management said underwriting has weakened across the market and, on the Q2 2026 call, described weaker covenants and more rollover risk across some players.
followups.uw_relevance: The company itself flags that private credit expansion could worsen losses among non-bank lenders, a concentrated credit loss area relevant to D&O review of credit oversight.

followups.question: How much of the FY2026 Q2 fee surge came from trading and deal activity that management expects will not repeat, and what is the expected level of noninterest income in the coming quarters?
followups.summary: Revenue rose 27.7% year on year in FY2026 Q2 and noninterest income reached 1.25x net interest income. Management said the equities result would be hard to repeat and that the environment was close to as good as it gets.
followups.uw_relevance: Trading and deal-driven fees are volatile, so the FY2026 Q2 earnings base may not persist, which matters when D&O reviewers read profitability.

followups.question: How will the planned increase in the quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share and the continued buybacks be funded if the G-SIB and Basel III changes raise required capital?
followups.summary: Share repurchases were $6.79B in FY2026 Q2, down from $8.32B in FY2026 Q1, and buybacks to net income fell to 0.32x from 0.50x. The board intends to increase the quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share, effective in the third quarter.
followups.uw_relevance: Heavy capital returns alongside higher expected capital requirements is a capital-allocation judgment that D&O reviewers weigh against the capital outlook.

followups.question: How have Middle East developments and higher energy prices affected trading risk, deal timing and consumer credit, and what drove the rise in average total VaR?
followups.summary: Management tied Middle East developments to deal timing and higher energy prices, and cited elevated gas prices and inflation as pressures on consumers. Average total VaR (95%) was $49M in FY2026 Q2 against $37M in FY2026 Q1.
followups.uw_relevance: Energy and geopolitical shocks flow into market volatility and credit losses, so management's own channel view is a reference point for D&O market-risk review.

followups.question: What security incidents have occurred since the breaches disclosed in the 10-K, and what controls address the AI-related increase in cyber risk that management described?
followups.summary: The 10-K states the firm has experienced security breaches from cyber attacks and that future breaches are inevitable. On the Q1 2026 call the CEO called cyber the firm's largest risk and said AI has made cyber risk worse and harder.
followups.uw_relevance: The disclosed history of breaches and management's ranking of cyber as the largest risk bear directly on D&O review of data security oversight.

followups.question: What succession plan covers the President and COO role after Daniel Pinto retires at the end of 2026, and how are responsibilities divided between the two Co-Presidents and the new CIB and CCB leaders?
followups.summary: Daniel Pinto, President and Chief Operating Officer, will retire at the end of 2026. Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh were named Co-Presidents on 25 June 2026, and Marianne Lake, former CCB CEO, is retiring.
followups.uw_relevance: Several senior changes within about a year, including the President and COO role, are a succession and key-person consideration for D&O underwriting review.

followups.question: What changes were made to supervision of the statutorily disqualified person after the SEC censure, and what is the status of the pending South Africa inquiry and the India fine under appeal?
followups.summary: The SEC censured JPMorgan Chase and its securities unit for failing to supervise a statutorily disqualified person who traded in the US without permission from late 2021 to early 2024. No fine was imposed, but a cease-and-desist order was issued, and other matters remain pending.
followups.uw_relevance: A supervisory failure finding with a cease-and-desist order is a regulatory conduct record relevant to D&O review of supervision and compliance controls, even without a fine.

followups.question: What integration, credit underwriting and operating controls will apply to the Apple Card portfolio during the roughly 24 months before closing, and what does the $2.2B footnoted in the provision line cover?
followups.summary: Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card. The forward purchase commitment was entered on 30 December 2025, with closing expected about 24 months later, and filings footnote $2.2B associated with the transaction in the provision line.
followups.uw_relevance: A large consumer credit portfolio acquisition with a long integration period adds credit and operational exposure that D&O reviewers track through closing.

followups.question: What drives the increase in the adjusted expense outlook, and how much of the higher expense is tied to revenue-related expense rather than to a change in the cost base?
followups.summary: On 14 July 2026 the firm raised its FY2026 NII excluding Markets outlook to about $96.5B from about $95B and its adjusted expense outlook to about $107.5B from about $105B, citing higher volume and revenue-related expense.
followups.uw_relevance: Higher expense guidance tied to revenue outperformance is a change to the operating plan that D&O reviewers weigh against the revenue outlook.

followups.question: What evidence supports the narrowed low single-digit consumer deposit growth outlook, and how are yield-seeking outflows being managed?
followups.summary: On the Q1 2026 call the expected range for 2026 consumer deposit growth was low to mid-single digits. On the Q2 2026 call it was low single-digit, with yield-seeking flows described as a continuing factor and probably a risk. Deposit growth year on year was 5.9% in FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: Deposit growth and funding stability bear on liquidity risk for a bank, and a narrowing outlook is a change in management's own funding view.

followups.question: What is the status of the civil suit filed in Florida state court naming JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. and the CEO, and what claims are asserted against the bank and the CEO?
followups.summary: A civil lawsuit filed in January 2026 in Florida state court by President Donald J. Trump, personally and through affiliated entities, names JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. and its CEO. The matter is listed as open in the filings reviewed.
followups.uw_relevance: Company-specific litigation that names the CEO directly creates D&O exposure to monitor while the case remains open.

metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks to net income fell to 0.32x in FY2026 Q2 from 0.50x in FY2026 Q1, versus 0.55x in FY2025. R3 ties the lower payout to the dividend increase, and it sits alongside the falling CET1 ratio in K1.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Share repurchases fell to $6.79B in FY2026 Q2 from $8.32B in FY2026 Q1, after $31.59B in FY2025. R3 links the slowdown to a planned rise in the quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share, and Q6 asks how both will be funded if capital rules tighten.
metric_relevance.cet1_ratio: CET1 fell from 15.7% in FY2024 Q4 to 14.2% in FY2026 Q2 and a preliminary 13.9% in FY2026 Q3. K1 and R8 show management planning for a 5.2% G-SIB requirement in 2028, making this the main capital pressure point.
metric_relevance.deposit_growth_yoy: Deposit growth slowed to 5.9% YoY in FY2026 Q2 from 7.2% in FY2026 Q1. Management narrowed its 2026 consumer deposit growth outlook to low single digits, and B2 notes yield-seeking flows as a probable risk.
metric_relevance.deposits: Total deposits reached $2,713.70B in FY2026 Q2, up from $2,559.32B at FY2025 Q4. R6 estimates $1,743.90B of these are uninsured, so the size of the funding base depends on the stability of uninsured balances.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity rose to $374.60B in FY2026 Q2 from $362.44B at FY2025 Q4. It is the base for ROE and the unrealized loss ratio, and K1 and R8 show that higher G-SIB requirements are measured against this capital base.
metric_relevance.fee_income_growth_yoy: Fee income grew 46.7% YoY in FY2026 Q2, following -20.9% in FY2025 Q2, which shows a cyclical swing. K7 notes that noninterest income reached 1.25x net interest income and that management expects the equities result to be hard to repeat.
metric_relevance.lcr: LCR fell to 110.0% in FY2026 Q2 from 112.0% in FY2026 Q1 and 113.0% in FY2025 Q2. K2 and R6 link this decline to rising uninsured deposits, which raises the question of funding stability under stress.
metric_relevance.loan_loss_reserve_ratio: The allowance to loans ratio was 1.8% in FY2026 Q2, down from 1.9% through FY2024 Q4 to FY2025 Q3. K8 sets this against nonperforming loans rising to 0.7% and lower card charge-off guidance, which Q3 asks management to explain.
metric_relevance.net_income: Net income was $21.16B in FY2026 Q2 and $15.30B in FY2026 Q3, while FY2025 totaled $57.05B against $58.47B in FY2024. Earnings are strong, but the FY2026 Q2 peak depends on the fee surge that K7 says may be partly pulled forward.
metric_relevance.nim: Net interest margin was 2.4% in FY2026 Q2 and 2.5% in FY2026 Q1, down from 2.7% in FY2023. R11 shows management raising its NII outlook on higher volume, so margin pressure may be offset by balance growth.
metric_relevance.noninterest_income: Noninterest income reached $31.84B in FY2026 Q2 from $24.47B in FY2026 Q1, against $87.00B for FY2025. K7 says the fee level is partly pulled forward, and B3 records management saying the environment was close to as good as it gets.
metric_relevance.npl_ratio: The nonperforming loan ratio rose to 0.7% at FY2025 Q4 from 0.5% at FY2023 Q4. K8 pairs this with lowered card net charge-off guidance of about 3.2%, and Q3 asks what supports that lower figure.
metric_relevance.revenue: Revenue was $57.35B in FY2026 Q2 and $50.17B in FY2026 Q3, against $45.80B in FY2025 Q4, so the top line is elevated. K7 flags the fee surge as partly pulled forward, so the current level may be hard to sustain.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: QoQ growth jumped to 15.1% in FY2026 Q2 after 8.8% in FY2026 Q1 and -1.4% in FY2025 Q4. B3 records management shifting to a cautious view after strong investment banking fees, so this spike may not persist.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: YoY growth of 27.7% in FY2026 Q2 follows -10.5% in FY2025 Q2, so the reported rate is distorted by a weak base. K7 says the equities result would be hard to repeat, which makes the spike a weak guide to trend.
metric_relevance.roa: ROA was 1.4% in FY2025, down from 1.5% in FY2024 and in line with 1.4% in FY2021. K10 presents profitability as sustained, but the figure does not show how much of the FY2026 quarterly earnings is tied to the fee surge.
metric_relevance.roe: ROE was 16.1% in FY2025 against 17.4% in FY2024, and K10 describes returns as sustained. Because ROE uses average equity, it is sensitive to equity growth as capital requirements rise.
metric_relevance.tier1_ratio: Tier 1 capital ratio declined from 16.8% in FY2024 Q4 to 15.1% in FY2026 Q2, on the same downward path as CET1. The fall is tied to the G-SIB and Basel III changes that R8 describes.
metric_relevance.uninsured_deposit_share: Uninsured deposits reached 64.3% of total deposits in FY2026 Q2, up from 60.9% at FY2025 Q4 and 56.1% at FY2023 Q4. K2 flags this alongside the weaker LCR, and Q2 asks how concentrated these balances are in the largest accounts.
metric_relevance.unrealized_loss_to_equity: Unrealized securities losses equal 4.9% of equity in FY2026 Q2, down from 7.8% at FY2024 Q4 and 12.6% at FY2022. It sits alongside the CET1 decline in K1 as a measure of balance-sheet capital strength.
